key_insight: Replace the static one-to-one link between vision encoders and LLMs with a dynamic many-to-many cross-layer injection so the language model can access hierarchical visual features at multiple depths, enabling better integration of local details and global semantics.
problem_solved: Current VLMs suffer a visual feature bottleneck from feeding only the vision encoder's final output into the LLM, which prevents comprehensive alignment with multi-scale visual information and limits accurate multimodal reasoning.
method: Introduce dynamic cross-layer injection that maps multiple layers of the vision encoder to multiple layers of the LLM (many-to-many) rather than a single output→input connection.
Use lightweight fusion adapters and dynamic gating/routing to selectively inject multi-scale visual tokens into appropriate LLM layers, preserving efficiency while enabling richer alignment.

Train with joint alignment objectives so hierarchical visual features (local patches, mid-level motifs, global scene) are matched to corresponding LLM representations for coherent multimodal reasoning.
impact: Enables LLMs to reason with finer-grained and hierarchical visual information, improving grounding, interpretability, and performance on complex multimodal tasks without major compute overhead from full cross-modal re-designs.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: one-to-one (single visual output → LLM input) vs many-to-many (multiple vision layers ↔ multiple LLM layers).
Architecture schematic showing vision encoder layers, fusion adapters, dynamic gates, and injected connections into LLM layers.
Illustration of hierarchical visual features (patch → region → scene) mapped to corresponding LLM processing stages (local → compositional → global).
Attention/activation heatmap example showing improved localization and cross-layer feature usage during a multimodal reasoning query.
paper_title: From One-to-One to Many-to-Many: Dynamic Cross-Layer Injection for Deep Vision-Language Fusion
paper_authors: Cheng Chen, Yuyu Guo, Pengpeng Zeng, Jingkuan Song, Peng Di
